answer_text: The evidence indicates that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) generally improves the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers, although one study reports a negative effect on a specific news benchmark. Most studies show that RAG reduces hallucination rates or increases answer accuracy compared to vanilla LLMs or no-retrieval baselines. Specifically, RAG was found to clearly reduce hallucinated content on science questions [S008, 0-960] and trivia questions [S010, 0-695]. It also made answers clearly more accurate on legal fact benchmarks [S020, 0-1074], scientific fact benchmarks [S015, 0-1128], and history benchmarks [S005, 0-975]. However, one study on news fact questions reported that retrieval augmentation made generated answers less accurate [S009, 0-1361].
